accepted.s: With reference to the composition of a State Legislative Council, which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Local authorities — One-third of the total membership
Registered graduates — One-sixth of the total membership
Teachers — One-third of the total membership
Members nominated by the Governor — One-twelfth of the total membership
accepted.x: One-third of the members of a Legislative Council are elected by local authorities. Graduates and teachers each elect one-twelfth, while the Governor nominates one-sixth.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure fraction and eliminate the swapped fractions.
accepted.sec: Legislative Council composition - elected fractions, nominated, size, tenure

accepted.s: The members of a State Legislative Council elected by registered graduates must represent graduates who have been on the electoral roll for at least
accepted.x: One-twelfth of a State Legislative Council is elected by registered graduates having at least three years' standing.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the closely related three-year qualifications in the composition rules.
accepted.sec: Legislative Council composition - elected fractions, nominated, size, tenure

accepted.s: The electorate consisting of teachers for a State Legislative Council comprises teachers who have taught for at least three years in institutions
accepted.x: One-twelfth of the Council is elected by teachers with at least three years' teaching experience in institutions not lower than the secondary-school level.
accepted.tq: Test the exact official qualification instead of a broader everyday meaning of teacher.
accepted.sec: Legislative Council composition - elected fractions, nominated, size, tenure

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the fields from which the Governor may nominate members to a State Legislative Council?
accepted.x: The nominated category includes literature, science, art, cooperative movement and social service. Agriculture taxation is not one of the constitutional fields.
accepted.tq: Find the outsider in the constitutionally specified list.
accepted.sec: Legislative Council composition - elected fractions, nominated, size, tenure

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding nomination to a State Legislative Council:
1. The Governor nominates one-sixth of the total members.
2. The nominated members represent literature, science, art, cooperative movement and social service.
3. Such nominations are made on the advice of the State Cabinet.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Governor nominates one-sixth of the Council from the specified fields, and the nominations are made on Cabinet advice.
accepted.tq: Check the fraction, the listed fields and the authority's advice together.
accepted.sec: Legislative Council composition - elected fractions, nominated, size, tenure

accepted.s: The members of a State Legislative Council are elected by which method?
o: Cumulative voting by the Legislative Assembly alone
First-past-the-post system by direct universal suffrage
Proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote
accepted.x: Members of a State Legislative Council are elected indirectly through proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the electoral system and the appointing authority.
accepted.sec: Legislative Council composition - elected fractions, nominated, size, tenure

accepted.s:
With reference to the size of a State Legislative Council, which of the following statements are correct?
1. Its membership cannot exceed one-third of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly.
2. Its membership cannot be less than 40.
3. Its actual strength is fixed by Parliament.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: A Legislative Council must have at least 40 members and cannot exceed one-third of the Assembly's strength. Parliament fixes its actual strength within these limits.
accepted.tq: Combine the two numerical limits with the authority that fixes the actual size.
accepted.sec: Legislative Council composition - elected fractions, nominated, size, tenure

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the tenure of the State Legislative Council?
o: It is a permanent body, and one-sixth of its members retire every year.
It is a permanent body, and one-third of its members retire every second year.
It is dissolved every five years along with the Assembly.
It has a fixed tenure of six years as a whole House.
accepted.x: The Legislative Council is a permanent House. One-third of its members retire every second year, while each member has a six-year term.
accepted.tq: Separate the tenure of an individual member from the continuity of the House.
accepted.sec: Legislative Council composition - elected fractions, nominated, size, tenure

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the Legislative Assembly from the Legislative Council in relation to a Money Bill?
o: A Money Bill may originate in either House, but the Council has the final decision.
The Council may reject a Money Bill if two-thirds of its members so decide.
A Money Bill can originate only in the Council on the Governor's recommendation.
A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Assembly, and the Council may make recommendations within 14 days.
accepted.x: A Money Bill is introduced only in the Legislative Assembly on the Governor's recommendation. The Council can only recommend changes and must return it within 14 days; it cannot reject or amend it.
accepted.tq: Identify who introduces, who recommends and who has the final word.
accepted.sec: Assembly vs Council - money bills, ordinary bills, delaying power, no joint sitting

accepted.s: In a State Legislature, the certificate that a Bill is a Money Bill is issued by the
accepted.x: Under Article 199(3), the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly certifies whether a Bill is a Money Bill.
accepted.tq: Apply the 'who would do this job?' method to the certification power.
accepted.sec: Assembly vs Council - money bills, ordinary bills, delaying power, no joint sitting

accepted.s: A Money Bill passed by the Legislative Assembly of a State is returned by the Legislative Council after 14 days with recommendations. What is the constitutional position?
o: The Governor decides which recommendations are binding.
The Bill lapses and must be introduced again.
The Assembly may accept or reject the recommendations.
The Assembly must accept all the recommendations.
accepted.x: The Council can only make recommendations on a Money Bill. The Assembly may accept or reject them, and the Council has no power to make its recommendations binding.
accepted.tq: Follow the Bill's route and distinguish recommendation from amendment power.
accepted.sec: Assembly vs Council - money bills, ordinary bills, delaying power, no joint sitting

accepted.s: An ordinary Bill passed by the Legislative Assembly and rejected by the Legislative Council is
o: Sent to Parliament for final decision
Automatically rejected by the State Legislature
Referred to a joint sitting of both Houses
Subject to the constitutional delaying procedure, after which the Assembly's will prevails
accepted.x: The Council cannot permanently veto an ordinary Bill passed by the Assembly. It may delay it for three months on the first occasion and one month on the second; thereafter the Assembly's will prevails.
accepted.tq: Track the delaying power rather than treating the Council's rejection as a veto.
accepted.sec: Assembly vs Council - money bills, ordinary bills, delaying power, no joint sitting

accepted.s: For how long can the Legislative Council delay an ordinary Bill passed by the Legislative Assembly on the first occasion and on the second occasion, respectively?
accepted.x: An ordinary Bill may be delayed by the Council for up to three months on the first occasion and one month on the second occasion.
accepted.tq: Keep the two successive delaying periods in their correct order.
accepted.sec: Assembly vs Council - money bills, ordinary bills, delaying power, no joint sitting

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Bill originating in the Legislative Council and rejected by the Legislative Assembly comes to an end.
2. The Legislative Council has no second chance to reconsider such a Bill.
3. A joint sitting can be summoned to resolve this disagreement in a State Legislature.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: a Bill originating in the Council ends when rejected by the Assembly, and there is no second chance for the Council. Statement 3 is false because State Legislatures have no provision for a joint sitting to resolve such a deadlock.
accepted.tq: Spot the Parliament–State Legislature confusion in the joint-sitting statement.
accepted.sec: Assembly vs Council - money bills, ordinary bills, delaying power, no joint sitting

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding demands for grants in a State Legislature is correct?
o: Demands for grants are voted by the Governor after discussion in the Council.
The Legislative Council votes on demands for grants, while the Assembly only discusses them.
Demands for grants are voted only in the Legislative Assembly, while the Council may discuss them.
Both Houses vote jointly on demands for grants.
accepted.x: The Legislative Assembly alone votes on demands for grants. The Legislative Council may discuss them but cannot vote on them.
accepted.tq: Separate the power to discuss from the power to vote.
accepted.sec: Assembly vs Council - money bills, ordinary bills, delaying power, no joint sitting

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the relative position of a State Legislative Council and the Rajya Sabha?
o: The State Council's power is essentially a delaying power and is weaker than that of the Rajya Sabha.
The State Council can dissolve the Legislative Assembly during a constitutional deadlock.
The State Council alone can ratify constitutional amendments.
The State Council has the same power as the Rajya Sabha to veto an ordinary Bill of the Assembly.
accepted.x: The State Legislative Council can delay legislation but cannot permanently veto an Assembly Bill. Its powers are considerably weaker than those of the Rajya Sabha in comparable matters.
accepted.tq: Avoid transferring the Rajya Sabha's powers to the State Council.
accepted.sec: Assembly vs Council - money bills, ordinary bills, delaying power, no joint sitting

accepted.s: Which statement concerning the representation of the Anglo-Indian community in State Legislative Assemblies is correct?
o: It was transferred to the Legislative Councils in 2020.
It was made compulsory in every State Assembly after 2020.
It continues without any constitutional change.
accepted.x: The constitutional provision for nomination of Anglo-Indian members to State Legislative Assemblies was discontinued in 2020.
accepted.tq: Test the time-bound constitutional change directly.
accepted.sec: Legislative Council composition - elected fractions, nominated, size, tenure

accepted.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, the Legislative Council strength was prescribed as not more than 50 members for Andhra Pradesh and 40 members for Telangana. The permissible strength for Andhra Pradesh was subsequently raised to
accepted.x: Section 22(1) of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act initially provided a ceiling of 50 members for Andhra Pradesh and 40 for Telangana. The 2015 Amendment Act raised Andhra Pradesh's permissible strength to 58.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the original ceiling from the figure introduced by the amendment.

accepted.s: Who is the present Speaker of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly?
accepted.x: Ch. Ayyanna Patrudu is the present Speaker of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly.
accepted.tq: Use the current office-holder carefully and distinguish it from the first woman Speaker.

accepted.x: The 2026 Monsoon Session of the Andhra Pradesh Legislature was notified to commence on 17 August 2026 under Article 174(1).
accepted.tq: Separate the date of notification from the date on which the session commenced.
